name: Unity web requests
goal: The arcade mode of the basketball game uses a Twitch overlay for players to use for throwing. The overlay has to be made invisible at times so players cannot shoot anymore.

approach.text:
As I have never used webrequests before, I looked up how web requests were sent. The following sources suggested to use a from:
<<source Technologies, U. (28-04-2023). Unity - Manual: Sending a form to an HTTP server (POST). https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/UnityWebRequest-SendingForm.html>>
<<source Technologies, U. (28-04-2023). Unity - Scripting API: Networking.UnityWebRequest.Put. https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Networking.UnityWebRequest.Put.html>>
My company mentor informed me as we were creating the script that the functions mentioned were Legacy functions, meaning they were intended for older versions.

With the following source, I managed to send web requests:
<<source How to write HTTP post request in Unity by using UnityWebRequest? (22-05-2019). Stack Overflow. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51926762/how-to-write-http-post-request-in-unity-by-using-unitywebrequest>>

The data consisted of just a string containing data in json format. As the company mentor mentioned that it was not the most versatile solution, we created a class to hold the data. The data did not make it to the overlay, as we discovered using the log. Using the following source, we serialized the data correctly: <<source Technologies, U. (28-04-2023). Unity - Manual:  JSON Serialization. https://docs.unity3d.com/2020.3/Documentation/Manual/JSONSerialization.html>>.

normalLearnings: I know how to send web requests in Unity.
I know how to serialize an object to a json string.

contribution: This directly contributes to the end product.
